overview.geometryNote: Zome on a 10-sided plan. Five horizontal bands of rhombic panels labelled z1 (apex) through z5 (widest, at the base), plus a base course of z4 half panels that fill the notches, a header panel over the doorway, and mirrored special panels down the door jambs. All struts are the same length; only the miter and bevel angles change from band to band. This is the same zome geometry as Trillium's Acorn Sauna, just stopped at the widest band instead of carrying past it.

strut.countNote: 251 is printed on the Exploded View sheet, but the identical figure appears on Trillium's 10'6 Acorn and 20' zome plans, which have different panel counts. Treat it as boilerplate and count off the panel schedule.

length.note: Identical for every regular panel edge and for every special-panel edge that lies on the zome surface.

crossSection.note: The plans publish no strut cross-section. Materials call for (21) 2x6x10' / 38x140x3m kiln-dried for the frame, and the builders method has you rip the strut stock in half on the table saw at the bevel angle. Finished section is builder-chosen; the jig is set to suit.

strut.bevelNote: There is no single bevel. Each band has a top bevel (the two struts pointing toward the apex) and a bottom bevel (the two pointing down/out). Where two bands meet the bevels match, so the numbers chain: 11.1 / 6.3 / 8 / 11.1 / 14.2 / 14.2. See panels[].bevels.
strut.miterNote: Every miter angle in these plans is stated OFF 90 degrees - the number is what you dial into the miter saw. Within one rhombus panel all four struts share the same miter.

midLength.note: Width across the panel at mid height; use it to set up the jig.

componentList.note: Transcribed exactly as printed. The same list is printed twice - once on the Exploded View (sheet 3) and again on its own on sheet 4.

sheetLayout.note: Three sheet-material options are offered, one per sheet (15, 16, 17): (16) 4x12 / 1.22 x 3.66 sheets, (10) 6x12 / 1.829 x 3.66 sheets, or (10) 6' x 90' / 1.829 x 27.5 m continuous roll. The text advises that unless you are covering with plywood as part of a conventional roof assembly you should use at least 4x12 sheets, and that roll goods such as Solexx are better still; longer runs waste less. Trillium offer to help source oversized polycarbonate.

pdfIssues.issue: The z5 miter is printed 15 deg in the panel table, but the plan's own z5 half sheet (sheet 7) prints 15.7 deg for the same corner, and 15.7 is what the printed dimensions give (5'-2 3/8" / 1584 mm mid length against the 3'-3 1/8" / 994 mm strut, and 3'-11 1/4" / 1200 mm across the z5 half). The table value has lost its decimal.

pdfIssues.sheet: Exploded View (sheet 3) and Component List (sheet 4), both units
pdfIssues.issue: Summary counts do not match the itemised list. Stated '53 reg panels' but z1 10 + z2 9 + z3 8 + z4 9 + z5 8 = 44. Stated '13 special panels' but z2 half 1 + z3 half vertical 2 + z4 half base 9 + z5 half 2 + header panel 1 = 15. Identical discrepancy to Trillium's 20' zome plan.
'251 struts' is printed here and also on Trillium's 10'6 Acorn and 20' zome plans, which have different panel counts. It cannot be right for all three.
pdfIssues.severity: moderate - do not order stock off this number

pdfIssues.issue: Sheet 4 is a text-only reprint of the component list already given on sheet 3. Nothing new; easy to mistake for a second, different list.

pdfIssues.sheet: Special Panels (sheet 8) vs Regular Panel Dimensions (sheet 5)
pdfIssues.issue: The header panel's top edge is printed 3'-11/16" (3'-0 11/16") / 931 mm while the z2 mid length it butts against is 3'-0 5/8" / 930 mm - a 1/16" / 1 mm mismatch. The z2 half's base is also printed 931 mm on the metric sheet 6 against 930 mm in the metric panel table.

pdfIssues.sheet: Base Sections - non-Beveled Method (sheet 10), both units
pdfIssues.issue: The note 'I have this set up so you rip a 2x10 section into 2 beveled base sections' is reprinted verbatim on the non-beveled sheet.

The deck is drawn as 10 sections although the base layout has 9 base sections plus an open door bay. No itemised cut list is given for the deck on this model (the 10'6 and 20' plans both include one).
Shelves are drawn for the non-beveled method only, with no equivalent for the beveled method, and no quantity is stated. The materials list also has no allowance for shelf or deck stock.

No strut cross-section is published anywhere. Builders have to infer it from the materials list (2x6 stock) plus the builders-method instruction to rip strut stock in half at the bevel angle. The method says other strut dimensions are fine as long as they are consistent and the bevel angle is accurate.

Compressed feet-inches notation is used without the zero: 3'-5/8" means 3'-0 5/8", 3'-11/16" means 3'-0 11/16", 7'-1/2" means 7'-0 1/2", 5'-1/4" means 5'-0 1/4", 2'- 1/4" means 2'-0 1/4". The door card width prints as 2'-4 5/16 and the shelf frame as 1'-10 3/4, both missing the closing inch mark.
